subject: Service integrity briefing — Oxbridge inference errors and remedial plan
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@oxbridge.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T08:12:05Z
Subject: Inference failures seen this morning (request for impact and next steps)

Hi Nikhil,

Quick heads-up — starting at ~07:45 UTC we saw a spike of malformed completions from the Redwood endpoint we use for our fraud-detection assistant. Examples: truncated responses mid-sentence, missing JSON fields in structured outputs, and a handful of 500 HTTPs from the API. Impact: roughly 7% of generation requests failed or returned invalid output between 07:45–08:20 UTC.

We’ve paused the feature on our side and captured request IDs; I included two request IDs below for triage: oxb-req-12045, oxb-req-12063. Can you confirm whether this was on your side and an ETA for a fix? We’re preparing a short incident note for our ops team and would appreciate an initial acknowledgment.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Engineering Lead, Integrations
Oxbridge Financial

Attachment: captured-requests.txt (3KB, request IDs + truncated responses)

I’m looping in Laura from Reliability who’s leading the on-call response. We’ll provide an initial incident summary and mitigation shortly. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your automation flows.

Best,

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T09:30:00Z
Subject: Internal: Oxbridge investigation notes and candidate RCA (internal)

Nikhil / Stephanie —

Investigation summary (internal-only):
- Timeline overview (UTC):
  * 07:40 — first error rate increase observed by internal telemetry (request latency + 500s).
  * 07:45 — Oxbridge reports malformed completions (request IDs received).
  * 07:46–08:05 — automated fallback routed requests to compatible replica; some cached KV lookups returned stale handles.
  * 08:07 — rollback of an autoscaling kernel selection made at 07:30 was applied; that remedied the majority of 500s.
- Root cause (preliminary): a cache eviction edge-case in the KV prefix cache that surfaced only under a burst of mid-sequence context updates. When the cache returned a stale descriptor, subsequent kernel code path presumed a valid KV mapping and produced truncated/invalid outputs for those in-flight requests.
- Scope: ~7% of requests across a subset of model variants served from the eu-west-1 pool between 07:40–08:20 UTC. No data exfiltration detected.
- Mitigation taken: forced cache invalidation for affected pools, revert of the autoscaling kernel change, and throttling applied to aggressive client bursts while we patched the eviction logic.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Patch: deploy fix for eviction logic (hotfix candidate v2026.10.31-kvfix) — ETA 2 business hours after code sign-off.
2) Validation: run synthetic load against eu-west-1 with mid-sequence updates to confirm no stale descriptors surface.
3) Customer comms: prepare a concise RCA and timeline for Oxbridge and any other affected customers (Nikhil will lead customer-facing note).
4) Postmortem: schedule cross-functional blameless postmortem and track action items in the incident tracker (DBL-9832).

Attachments: timeline-export.log (trimmed), diagnostic-snippet.txt

Laura
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@oxbridge.com>, Claire Morris <claire.morris@oxbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:05:00Z
Subject: Service integrity briefing — Oxbridge inference errors and remedial plan

Hi Daniel / Claire —

Thank you again for the report and for your patience while we completed our investigation. Below is a concise customer-facing post-incident summary including the root cause, verified timeline, and corrective actions we’ve committed to. If you’d prefer a short run-through call, I can schedule one for today.

Executive summary
- Impact: Between 07:40–08:20 UTC on 2026-10-30, approximately 7% of your inference requests routed to eu-west-1 experienced either HTTP 500s or malformed/truncated completions. We understand this affected your automated assistant flows.
- Root cause: A cache eviction edge-case in our prefix/KV caching layer that, under a tight burst pattern with mid-sequence updates, returned stale descriptors leading to truncated outputs for in-flight requests.
- Scope: Affected traffic was limited to specific model variants in eu-west-1. No customer data was exposed or altered beyond the returned truncated outputs.

Verified timeline (UTC)
- 07:40 — internal telemetry uptick (error rate + latency).
- 07:45 — Oxbridge alert received (you provided request IDs: oxb-req-12045, oxb-req-12063).
- 07:46 — on-call team began triage; automated fallback routes activated for some traffic.
- 07:50 — temporary throttles and forced cache invalidation applied to eu-west-1 pool.
- 08:07 — rollback of an autoscaling kernel selection completed; majority of 500s subsided.
- 08:20 — incident declared contained; monitoring remained on elevated watch for 24 hours.

Immediate actions completed
- Forced cache invalidation for the affected pools (07:50 UTC).
- Rollback of the kernel selection change (08:07 UTC).
- Throttling applied to aggressive client bursts while we validated the fix.
- Hotfix (v2026.10.31-kvfix) deployed to eu-west-1 and validated against synthetic loads (deployed 2026-10-31 11:15 UTC).

Committed next steps and timelines
1) Engineering patch and QA validation — completed: eviction fix deployed and validated; we will include the patch in the next stable runtime release.
2) Monitoring rule update — by 2026-11-05: create a dedicated alert for mid-sequence KV descriptor anomalies.
3) Client guidance — by 2026-11-03: publish short best-practice notes for safe mid-sequence context updates and recommended retry/backoff patterns.
4) Postmortem and action tracker — by 2026-11-10: full cross-functional postmortem and assignment of tracked action items in DBL-9832.

Attachments included for your review
- oxbridge-rca-diagram.pdf — a diagram of the cache eviction scenario and affected code path.
- remediation-schedule.xlsx — timeline and owners for the corrective actions.
- timeline-export.log — trimmed telemetry extract (sanitized).

If you’d like a quick walk-through, I can set up a 30-minute call with Laura (Reliability) and Stephanie (Product) this afternoon.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’re committed to making this right and preventing recurrence.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference | reliability@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187
